title: focus_seconds_reported is always 0 in the real submit flow: the review page's submit form has no _focus_seconds input (only the per-question form does), and the integration test injects the field manually, masking the gap
evidence:
form_pages.gleam (view_review, the submit form): "form_view.view_honeypot_field(),
            form_view.view_timing_field(
              loaded_at_ms: form_view.current_unix_ms(),
            ),
            html.button(
              [
                attribute.type_("submit")," ... form_question_pages.gleam:88 (per-question form only): "attribute.name("_focus_seconds")," ... form_handler.gleam:1262-1263: "fn parse_focus_seconds(values: List(#(String, String))) -> Int {
  case application_handler.get_form_value(values, "_focus_seconds") {" ... form_handler.gleam:839: "focus_seconds: parse_focus_seconds(values)," ... reference_exit_routes_integration_test.gleam:174: "|> simulate.form_body([#("_focus_seconds", "240"), ..timing_fields()])"
detail: The submit POST originates from the review page, which never renders _focus_seconds (reference_form.js only fills [data-focus-seconds] on the question form). parse_focus_seconds returns 0 for the missing value, so fraud_signals.form_session.focus_seconds_reported is always 0 in production, contradicting the dev record's claim 'rc3-4 captures focus_seconds_reported'.
recommended_fix: Add a hidden _focus_seconds input (value 0, data-focus-seconds) to the review page's submit form, or persist focus seconds server-side across the session and read them at submit.

title: character_verification omits free_text_signals[] which the spec's per-slot mapping lists for character_ref (landlord and employer blocks both carry it)
evidence:
result.gleam:166-171 (character_verification, 6 entries ending at): "#("would_stand_again", str_or_null(draft, "would_stand_again")),
  ])" ... result.gleam:139 (landlord) and :158 (employer): "#("free_text_signals", free_text_signals(draft))," ... spec: "**`character_ref`**: `identity_confirmed`, `relationship{+capacity}`, `known_duration`, `character_statement`, `would_stand_again`, `free_text_signals[]`."
detail: The character slot has no free_text question (questions.gleam character_questions ends at would_stand_again), so the array would always be empty — impact is nil today, but the spec contract lists the field and the other two slots emit it.
recommended_fix: Add #("free_text_signals", free_text_signals(draft)) to character_verification for shape parity with the spec, or note the deliberate omission in the spec.

title: An objected row renders the 'declined' state page: the classifier maps Refused | Objected -> Declined, so an objector re-visiting the token sees 'This reference was declined.'
evidence:
form_handler.gleam:98: "Refused | Objected -> Declined" ... form_copy.gleam:161-163: "pub const declined_title = "This reference was declined."
pub const declined_body = "No further messages will come from us.""
detail: AC4's re-tap flow redirects to the GET state page; the objector (who asked to stop contact, not declined) is told the reference 'was declined' — factually wrong copy in an honest-first design.
recommended_fix: Split Declined into refused/objected state pages (or branch view_declined's copy on status) so objected rows render objection-appropriate copy.
